extracted.intended_audience: cultural heritage organizations and institutions applying for NEH Division of Collections & Infrastructure grants (archives, libraries, museums, historical societies, university special collections)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and program-level criteria for preparing grant applications to NEH’s Division of Collections & Infrastructure, which funds preservation, access (including digital), challenge/match programs, endowments, and related projects for humanities collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve and provide access to humanities collections
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH’s Division of Collections & Infrastructure makes grants to organizations that seek to address the physical deterioration of their humanities collections as well as to provide access to them, including through digital methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should result in cultural resources that are easy to find and use, and that are preserved for future generations. Proposals that integrate preservation treatment with plans for access (physical and/or digital) align with the Division’s goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce new tools/methods and develop skilled practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: The division’s grant programs result in ... new tools and methods in preservation and access and knowledgeable and skilled cultural heritage practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funded projects are expected not only to preserve collections but also to advance preservation/access practice and workforce capacity—e.g., developing methodologies, technologies, training, or documentation that benefit the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge awards matching requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenge awards typically require the recipient to raise one to four dollars in new donations from non-federal sources for each federal dollar received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenge programs are designed to strengthen financial stability and require applicants to demonstrate fundraising capacity/strategy and the ability to leverage federal funds for long-term impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collections Stewardship program purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: This program funds projects to preserve and make available physical and digital collections important for research, teaching, and public engagement in the humanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should demonstrate that the collections and proposed activities have clear value for research, teaching, or public engagement and include realistic plans for preservation and access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rediscovering Our Revolutionary Tradition focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserves and improves access to primary sources that pertain to the establishment and expansion of the nation and the history of American government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority is on projects that document, preserve, and broaden access to primary sources related to the founding and development of the United States and its government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Celebrate America!/Chairman's Grants focus and amount
rubrics_metrics.description: Through this program, NEH will award 250 challenge grants of up to $25,000 each for projects that focus on the founding of the American nation, key historical figures, and milestones that reflect the exceptional achievements of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should center on specified subject matter (founding, key figures, milestones) and be structured to meet the challenge-grant matching model; note the stated maximum award amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endowments for Advancing the Humanities term and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides funds for 20-year term endowments to support long-term work in the humanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This program supports establishing/supplementing endowed funding with long-term sustainability expectations; applicants should propose durable, long-range plans consistent with a 20-year endowment model.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Digital Newspaper Program scope and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A partnership between NEH and the Library of Congress to create a national digital resource of historically significant newspapers published between 1690 and 1963, from all the states and U.S. territories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should focus on digitizing historically significant newspapers within the specified date range and contribute to a geographically broad, national resource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save America's Treasures eligibility (national significance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support preservation and/or conservation work on nationally significant historic collections and properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must demonstrate the national significance of the collections or properties and propose preservation/conservation work appropriate to that level of significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Notices of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: These suggestions augment guidance from a 2008 article ... As emphasized there, none of this is intended to supersede instructions found in application guidelines (aka Notices of Funding Opportunity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow the specific requirements and instructions in the current NOFO for each program; the page’s tips are supplemental and do not replace formal application rules, eligibility, deadlines, or required materials.
